scenes.visual: Title card: One Signal, Three Routes.

scenes.tts: A rat hears a tone that once came just before a mild shock. What does its brain do with that tone?
scenes.visual: A rat in a small chamber. A speaker icon emits a tone wave. Title card: One signal, three routes.
scenes.narration: A rat hears a tone that once came just before a mild shock. What does its brain do with that tone?

scenes.tts: Two things happen at once. The rat stops moving, and its blood pressure rises.
scenes.visual: The rat goes still (label: freezing). A pressure gauge beside it climbs (label: blood pressure).
scenes.narration: Two things happen at once. The rat stops moving, and its blood pressure rises.

scenes.tts: Neither one is the feeling of fear. But both can be measured, and that lets us trace them in the brain.
scenes.visual: A thought bubble with a question mark is crossed out; the freezing label and the gauge stay lit.
scenes.narration: Neither one is the feeling of fear. But both can be measured, and that lets us trace them in the brain.

scenes.tts: First, is the response learned? One group of rats hears tones that end in a shock.
scenes.visual: Group A: tone icon followed immediately by a lightning icon, repeated on a timeline.
scenes.narration: First, is the response learned? One group of rats hears tones that end in a shock.

scenes.tts: A second group gets the same tones and the same shocks, but kept apart in time.
scenes.visual: Group B: the same tone and lightning icons, spaced far apart on a timeline. Label: unpaired control.
scenes.narration: A second group gets the same tones and the same shocks, but kept apart in time.

scenes.tts: Later, the paired rats freeze far more to the tone alone. That difference is our estimate of what was learned.
scenes.visual: Two bars, tall for paired and short for unpaired, no numbers. The gap between them is shaded and labelled: learned.
scenes.narration: Later, the paired rats freeze far more to the tone alone. That difference is our estimate of what was learned.

scenes.tts: Where is it learned? The tone travels to the amygdala, a cluster of nuclei deep in the brain.
scenes.visual: A side view of a rat brain. A wave travels from the ear through the thalamus to a glowing almond-shaped amygdala.
scenes.narration: Where is it learned? The tone travels to the amygdala, a cluster of nuclei deep in the brain.

scenes.tts: The lateral amygdala is the input stage. The central amygdala sends the signal out.
scenes.visual: The amygdala enlarges into two boxes: lateral amygdala (input) with an arrow to central amygdala (output).
scenes.narration: The lateral amygdala is the input stage. The central amygdala sends the signal out.

scenes.tts: Three routes leave it. One runs to the periaqueductal gray, in the midbrain. It drives freezing.
scenes.visual: Arrow 1 from the central amygdala to the midbrain, labelled periaqueductal gray, ending in a freezing-rat silhouette.
scenes.narration: Three routes leave it. One runs to the periaqueductal gray, in the midbrain. It drives freezing.

scenes.tts: A second runs to the lateral hypothalamus. It drives the rise in blood pressure.
scenes.visual: Arrow 2 to the lateral hypothalamus, ending in a pressure gauge.
scenes.narration: A second runs to the lateral hypothalamus. It drives the rise in blood pressure.

scenes.tts: A third, mostly indirect, reaches a hormone chain: hypothalamus, pituitary, adrenal. In people, its hormone is cortisol.
scenes.visual: Arrow 3, dashed (mostly indirect), to the paraventricular nucleus, then a chain of three boxes: hypothalamus, pituitary, adrenal. A hormone droplet labelled cortisol (corticosterone in rats).
scenes.narration: A third, mostly indirect, reaches a hormone chain: hypothalamus, pituitary, adrenal. In people, its hormone is cortisol.

scenes.tts: Two of these routes are fast. Freezing and the pressure rise appear while the tone is still playing.
scenes.visual: A clock face with a fast-moving second hand appears under arrows 1 and 2. A tone bar runs along the bottom.
scenes.narration: Two of these routes are fast. Freezing and the pressure rise appear while the tone is still playing.

scenes.tts: The hormone route is slow. The adrenal must make its hormone, so levels peak tens of minutes later. Feedback then turns further release down.
scenes.visual: Under arrow 3 a clock with a minute hand sweeps slowly. A curve rises after a lag, peaks, then settles back toward a continuing low baseline, not to zero. Label: feedback limits release.
scenes.narration: The hormone route is slow. The adrenal must make its hormone, so levels peak tens of minutes later. Feedback then turns further release down.

scenes.tts: So here is the rule. A learned threat cue reaches the amygdala, then leaves by separate routes.
scenes.visual: The whole map is shown at once. On screen: one node, separate routes; two fast, one slow.
scenes.narration: So here is the rule. A learned threat cue reaches the amygdala, then leaves by separate routes.

scenes.tts: In this rat task, damaging neurons in one target impaired mainly its own response. Damage to the amygdala can impair both.
scenes.visual: A scissors icon cuts at the caudal periaqueductal gray (label: caudal PAG neurons): the freezing label dims while the gauge stays up. Reset. Scissors cut the central amygdala: freezing and the gauge both dim. Small label: a simplified model; the hormone branch was not measured here.
scenes.narration: In this rat task, damaging neurons in one target impaired mainly its own response. Damage to the amygdala can impair both.

scenes.tts: This map is for learned responses to a cue outside the body, measured in rats.
scenes.visual: A frame drawn around the map. Label: learned, outside cue, rats.
scenes.narration: This map is for learned responses to a cue outside the body, measured in rats.

scenes.tts: It does not say what the rat feels. Later chapters show where the map stops.
scenes.visual: The frame around the map stays. A thought bubble with a question mark sits outside it.
scenes.narration: It does not say what the rat feels. Later chapters show where the map stops.

scenes.tts: The amygdala is needed to learn the threat. Separate routes carry out the response, two fast and one slow.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: The amygdala is needed to learn the threat. Separate routes respond: two fast, one slow. A simplified map.
scenes.narration: The amygdala is needed to learn the threat. Separate routes carry out the response, two fast and one slow.

scenes.visual: End card with the takeaway line.
